description.narrative:
Overall objective The overall objective of the project is to stimulate inclusive sustainable economic growth with a special focus on EE appliances and industrial processes.
The project comprises three outcomes, each designed to achieve specific objectives. Outcome 1 - The uptake of Energy Efficient Appliances in Zimbabwe has increased through national policy and capacity-building interventions as well as private sector development, linked to the regional EELA Project: The objective is to increase the adoption of energy-efficient appliances in Zimbabwe, thereby reducing poverty and mitigating adverse environmental impacts. The project will improve the policy and regulatory framework, strengthen capacity, and enhance private sector investments, particularly focusing on the development of the ESCO market and local value chains.
Outcome 2 - A Private Sector Industry Clean Tech Platform (ICTP) is set up to accelerate investments in the low-carbon transformation of the industrial sector targeting high impact industries: The goal is to set up a platform for identifying and promoting clean technology solutions within the industrial sector. The ICTP aims to stimulate economic growth, job creation, and environmental sustainability by supporting industries in introducing energy management systems and facilitating access to suitable technology and financing opportunities. High impact industries which will act as champions will be identified during the inception period.
Outcome 3 Effective e-waste management promoted and institutional capacity to manage and regulate e-waste is enhanced. The aim is to facilitate the development of effective e-waste management policies and practices in Zimbabwe focusing on repair, maintenance and end-of-life treatment of energy-efficient equipment. This will be achieved through a comprehensive market and feasibility report, policy advice and targeted capacity building.

Energieffektivitet för hållbar försörjning i Afrika (EELA) i Zimbabwe syftar till att stimulera en inkluderande och hållbar ekonomisk tillväxt i landet genom ett integrerat projekt för energieffektivitet (EE) som syftar till att påskynda införandet av energieffektivitetsbelysning och apparater, samt att inrikta sig på investeringar i en koldioxidsnål omvandling av industrisektorn och i lokala värdekedjor. hantering av e-avfall och därmed sammanhängande kapacitetsuppbyggnad och medvetandehöjande åtgärder. Projektet tar upp utmaningar relaterade till ökad efterfrågan på el, apparaters livscykler, lokala värdekedjor och miljöförstöring orsakad av ineffektiva energimetoder. EELA Zimbabwe-projektet är en del av ett programmatiskt tillvägagångssätt som inkluderar det regionala EELA-projektet och flera landsfönster, med EELA Zimbabwe som ett "landsfönster", efter förebild av EELA-landsprojekten i Kenya och Zambia. EELA Zimbabwe har tre efterfrågade resultat, nämligen: - Resultat 1 - Användningen av EE-apparater i Zimbabwe har ökat genom nationella politiska och kapacitetsbyggande insatser samt utveckling av den privata sektorn, kopplat till det regionala EELA-projektet - Resultat 2 - En plattform för ren teknik inom den privata sektorn (ICTP) inrättas för att påskynda investeringar i den koldioxidsnåla omställningen av industrisektorn - Resultat 3 - Effektiv hantering av e-avfall främjas och institutionell kapacitet att hantera och reglera e-avfall förbättras.

The Energy Efficiency for Sustainable Livelihoods in Africa (EELA) Zimbabwe Country Window aims to stimulate inclusive and sustainable economic growth in the country through an integrated Energy Efficiency (EE) project targeting the accelerated uptake of EE lighting and appliances, as well as targeting investments in the low-carbon transformation of the industrial sector and in local value chains, e-waste management and related capacity building and awareness raising. The project addresses challenges related to increasing electricity demand, appliance life cycles, local value chains and environmental degradation caused by inefficient energy practices.
The EELA Zimbabwe project is part of a programmatic approach including the regional EELA project and multiple country windows, with EELA Zimbabwe as a “country window”, following the example of the EELA country projects in Kenya and Zambia.
EELA Zimbabwe has three outcomes namely: - Outcome 1 - The uptake of EE Appliances in Zimbabwe has increased through national policy and capacity building interventions as well as private sector development, linked to the regional EELA Project - Outcome 2 - A Private Sector Industry Clean Tech Platform (ICTP) is set up to accelerate investments in the low-carbon transformation of the industrial sector - Outcome 3 – Effective e-waste management promoted and institutional capacity to manage and regulate e-waste is enhanced.
